# forgesworn/gopherkind

> Gopherholes served from Nostr relays. Documents are addressable Nostr
> events (kind 31436, named for RFC 1436); a bridge daemon serves them
> over gopher (RFC 1436), Gemini and HTTP from the same events.
> Virtual holes render any npub's kind 0 profile, kind 1 notes and
> NIP-23 long-form articles as browsable gopherspace with no publishing
> required. TypeScript on Node >= 24, one runtime dependency
> (nostr-tools, pinned 2.23.9).
>
> Formerly named burrow; renamed before first release, so no published
> version ever carried the old name.

## Event format

- kind `31436`, addressable. One event per document.
- exactly one `d` tag: a valid absolute path; root menu is `/`. Paths
  are byte-exact identifiers and are never normalised.
- exactly one `type` tag: `0` text or `1` menu. Missing, duplicate or
  unrecognised required tags make the event invalid.
- zero or one `title` tag. Gopherkind validation and NIP-40 `expiration`
  are checked after the NIP-01 winner is selected; a malformed or expired
  winner makes the path absent and an available older revision is not selected
  instead. A relay may delete an expired winner, so expiration alone is not a
  durable tombstone for a coordinate with older history.
- Menu content is a "kindmap": gophermap lines with host/port columns
  removed. `<itemtype><display>\t<link>` per line; lines without a tab
  are info text. Links: same-hole `/path`, `npub1`/`nprofile1`
  (their hole root), `naddr1` (kind 31436 document, or kind 30023
  article served at `/articles/<naddr>`), `gopher://host/T/selector`,
  or `http(s)://`/`gemini://` (served as an `h`/`URL:` item). Optional `nostr:`
  prefix on entities.

## Selector namespace (gopher and gemini alike)

- empty / `/`: bridge welcome menu
- `/<npub>`: hole root (authored `d=/`, else virtual root)
- `/<npub>/<path>`: document at that path
- gopher search: type 7 with tab-separated query
- Gemini and HTTP search: `/_gopherkind/search/<npub>`; `/<npub>/search`
  remains an ordinary authored document
- virtual paths when no authored document matches: `/profile.txt`,
  `/notes`, `/notes/<event-id>`, `/articles`, `/articles/<naddr>`,
  `/follows` (kind 3 contacts as a menu of holes), `/followers`
  (authors of kind 3 events tagging them; a sample, not a count)
- gopher personal menu, loopback only, never advertised or served
  remotely: `/me`, `/me/feed`, `/me/notes`, `/me/follows`,
  `/me/followers`, `/me/post` (type 7, search string is the note),
  `/me/delete/<id>` (type 7, must type "delete"). Identity comes from
  the connection origin, not from anything sent over the wire.
- gopher proxy: `/gopher/<host>[:port]/<type>/<selector>` on the HTTP
  frontend fetches and renders traditional gopherspace, rewriting
  links to stay inside the proxy
- gemini identity (client certificates + NIP-46, bridge never holds a
  user key): `/account`, `/pair` (bunker:// paste), `/pair/connect`
  (nostrconnect cross-device), `/post` (kind 1 via remote signer),
  `/feed` (kind 3 follows as a menu), `/unpair`. Gopher is read-only
  by design; the protocol cannot carry credentials safely.
- http frontend (default port 8070, aimed at lynx: plain HTML, real
  forms, no JavaScript): same hole paths plus `/go`, `/account`,
  `/pair`, `/post`, `/feed`, `/delete`, `/_gopherkind/search/<npub>?q=`. Loopback
  requests are trusted as the operator and use the CLI's signer, so
  local browsing needs no login; remote visitors pair via form and get
  a session cookie. Plain HTTP, so terminate TLS in front of it.

## CLI

The CLI is a complete client; the Gemini frontend is for visitors who
have no shell on the bridge host. Install: `npx @forgesworn/gopherkind`
(Node >= 24).

- interactive browser: `gopherkind` (bare, on a TTY) or
  `gopherkind browse [target]`. Numbered links, `back`/`up`/`reload`,
  `mark`/`marks`/`unmark <n>` bookmarks (state dir `bookmarks.json`),
  `history`, `go <target>`, `search <query>` (NIP-50 on holes, type 7
  on gopher), `feed` as a navigable menu, `post <text>` via the
  resolved signer, `$PAGER` for long documents. Targets: npub[/path],
  `nostr:` entities (npub/nprofile/naddr), NIP-05 names
  (someone@example.org[/path]), `gopher://` urls, bare hostnames. A `gopher://` url whose selector starts with an npub is
  recognised as a gopherkind bridge and browsed natively via relays;
  gophermap lines with npub selectors or `nostr:` h-links likewise.
- read (no identity needed): `gopherkind read <npub[/path]>`,
  `gopherkind read gopher://host/T/selector`,
  `gopherkind search <npub> <query>`,
  `gopherkind search gopher://host/7/selector <query>` (e.g. Veronica-2)
- write: `gopherkind post <text> [--dry-run]`, `gopherkind feed [--limit 20]`,
  `gopherkind delete <id|note1|nevent1> [--wide] [--reason x]` (NIP-09)
- identity: `gopherkind pair <bunker://...>`, `gopherkind unpair`,
  `gopherkind whoami`. Signer resolution order: `GOPHERKIND_NSEC` local key,
  then `GOPHERKIND_BUNKER` one-off URI, then the stored pairing.
- all commands take `[--relay wss://...]...` and `[--state-dir d]`
- `gopherkind serve [--port 7070] [--gemini-port 1965] [--host 0.0.0.0]
  [--hostname x] [--public-port n] [--relay wss://...]...
  [--pin npub1...]... [--cert f --key f] [--state-dir ~/.gopherkind]
  [--no-gemini] [--no-virtual] [--no-identity]`
- `gopherkind publish <dir> [--relay ...] [--expire 30d] [--dry-run]`,
  signs with `GOPHERKIND_NSEC` (nsec or 64-hex). Text files become type 0;
  `index.map`/`gophermap` become their directory's menu; other `*.map`
  files become menus at their own path.
- `gopherkind unpublish </path>... | --all [--dry-run]`: NIP-09 kind 5
  deletion request with `e`, `a` and `k` tags.

## Implementation notes

- Disk state is the Gemini TLS cert plus `pairings.json` (cert
  fingerprint -> bunker binding, mode 600) in the state dir; nothing
  else. Every NIP-46 call is per-request with a hard timeout.
- `src/secretguard.ts` blocks credential-shaped content (bunker://,
  nostrconnect://, nsec, ncryptsec, `secret=`) on both the /post path
  and CLI publish, before anything is signed.
- One-shot relay queries only (querySync), never live subscriptions.
- Per-IP token bucket (20 burst, 1/s refill), TTL+LRU caches (1 to 10
  minutes by type), NIP-50 search merged with client-side grep.
- Source layout: `selector.ts` (parse) -> `router.ts` (resolve to
  protocol-neutral Content) -> `render.ts` (gopher) / `gemtext.ts`
  (gemini). `virtual.ts` builds virtual holes, `fetch.ts` talks to
  relays, `publish.ts` is the CLI's write path. `target.ts` parses
  client-side targets (npub/nostr:/gopher://), `gopherclient.ts`
  fetches traditional gopherspace, `browse.ts` is the interactive
  terminal client.
- Published to npm as `@forgesworn/gopherkind` with a compiled `dist/`
  (Node refuses type stripping under node_modules); development runs
  straight from `src/` with no build step.
